predecessors.name: Land Chenla
predecessors.text: Land (Upper) Chenla north of the Tonlé Sap and along the Mekong, taken in Jayavarman II's unification

predecessors.name: Water Chenla
predecessors.text: Water (Lower) Chenla in the south, up to the Mekong delta

successors.name: Post-Angkor Cambodia
successors.text: the Khmer realm that remained after 1375: the Tonlé Sap basin and the Mekong lands, with the court at Phnom Penh (Chaktomuk) after Angkor was abandoned

successors.name: Lan Xang
successors.text: the northern Khmer lands that Cliopatria hands to Lan Xang in 1363

successors.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
successors.text: the western strip that Cliopatria hands to Ayutthaya in 1375

ledger.x: 802: Jayavarman II is consecrated at Mahendraparvata (Phnom Kulen) and the Khmer Empire begins. the page says he was proclaimed 'devaraja' at a consecration on Mount Mahendraparvata 'in 802', a consecration that 'set the foundation of the Angkor period'; the Khmer Empire page: 'lasted from 802 to 1431 AD'.
803: the Chenla lands join Jayavarman II. he returned 'to his home in the former kingdom of Chenla' and defeated 'a series of competing kings' (undated); the page is silent on Land Chenla by name.
803: Water Chenla joins.
c. 835: the court moves from Mahendraparvata to Hariharalaya near Roluos ('founded in the following years' after 802; infobox 'mid 9th century'). The year is a bridge between the two phrases.
875: the Khmer shape loses its eastern strip to Champa.
889: the court settles at Yasodharapura (Angkor), founded under Yasovarman I, 'reigned 889-915'; infobox 'Yasodharapura (late 9th century-928)'.
928: Jayavarman IV moves the capital to Lingapura (Koh Ker), infobox 'Lingapura (928-944)'.
944: Rajendravarman II restores Yasodharapura as the capital, infobox 'Yasodharapura (944-1431)'.
946: Angkor gained Rāmaññadesa 'in 946' (Sukhothai Kingdom page).
1006: Lavo stops being a tributary and is governed from Angkor (annexation, next event).
1006: Suryavarman I takes Lavo.
1052: Lavo returns to a ruler of its own.
1132: Khmer and Cham armies together 'briefly seized Nghệ An and raided Thanh Hoá's coast' against Đại Việt (Suryavarman II's second attempt after the 1128 rout at Nghệ An).
1136: a Vietnamese force of 30,000 under Đỗ Anh Vũ counterattacks into Khmer territory and retreats; the Cham make peace with Đại Việt and refuse to join Suryavarman's next attack, which fails.
1145: Suryavarman II invades Champa, sacks Vijaya and deposes Jaya Indravarman III ('The Khmers held Vijaya until 1149', Khmer Empire page).
1149: Jaya Harivarman I besieges Vijaya and defeats Prince Harideva at Mahisa; 'This ended Khmer occupation of northern Champa'.
1177: a Cham fleet sails up the Mekong to the Tonlé Sap, sacks Yasodharapura and kills King Tribhuvanadityavarman; 'The Cham then occupied Cambodia for about four years'.
1181: Jayavarman VII wins a decisive naval battle and expels the Cham; he is crowned king the same year ('in 1181 was crowned king himself', Jayavarman VII page).
1181: Lavo comes under Angkor again.

1188: the southern lands of Haripunjaya (Tak and the upper Ping) pass to Angkor in Cliopatria's shapes; the page is silent on any such conquest and the Haripunjaya dossier records the same event at conf 1.

1188: Jayavarman VII's empire reaches its widest extent short of Champa: he 'expanded Khmer control of the Mekong Valley northward to Vientiane' and 'southward down the Kra Isthmus'; infobox area 1,000,000 km2 for 1181-1218.
1190: Jayavarman VII's army under the Cham prince Vidyanandana 'defeated the Chams, occupied Vijaya, and captured Jaya Indravarman IV'; the Khmer Empire table dates the conquest 1190-1191.
1191: a revolt at Vijaya drives out Suryajayavarman; Vidyanandana retakes it, kills the two Jaya Indravarmans and 'declared independence from the Khmer Empire'.
1192: Jayavarman VII's invasions of Champa begin: 'repeated invasions' in 1192, 1195, 1198-1199 and 1201-1203.
1203: after 22 years of war the Khmer 'conquered large parts of their territory' (Khmer Empire page); the Chams are defeated, Vidyanandana flees to Đại Việt and a puppet government is set up.
1203: Champa becomes a Khmer province.
1218: Lavo leaves Angkor.
1220: the Khmer withdraw from Champa.
1238: Sukhothai breaks away.
1353: Angkor falls to Ayutthaya.
1357: Suryavamsa Rajadhiraja retakes the throne and ends the Siamese rule at Angkor.
1363: the northern lands pass to Lan Xang in Cliopatria's shapes.
1375: a western strip passes to Ayutthaya in Cliopatria's shapes (212 of the 215 cells lost lie in its Ayutthaya shape of 1375).
1393: Ramesuan of Ayutthaya besieges Angkor.
1394: Angkor is captured by Ayutthaya; the page does not say how long the Siamese held it or on what terms.
1431: Angkor falls and the Khmer Empire ends.

wars.name: Khmer-Cham war of c. 950
wars.outcome: Rajendravarman II's army pillaged the Po Nagar temple at Kauthara and took its golden Bhagavati statue, but the invasion ended in a 'bloody defeat'; Champa kept Kauthara.

wars.name: Khmer-Cham war of 1074-1080
wars.outcome: A Khmer army attacked Vijaya and other northern Cham centres in 1080 and was driven out by Harivarman IV, whose raiders later reached Sambor and the Mekong.

wars.name: Suryavarman II's wars against Đại Việt
wars.outcome: A Khmer force of 20,000 was routed in Nghệ An in 1128; with Cham help the Khmer briefly took Nghệ An in 1132; a Vietnamese counterattack in 1136 and the Cham peace with Đại Việt ended the effort.

wars.name: Khmer invasion of Champa (Suryavarman II)
wars.outcome: Suryavarman II sacked Vijaya in 1145 and the Khmer held northern Champa until Jaya Harivarman I retook Vijaya in 1149; he killed the pretender Vamsaraja at Mỹ Sơn in 1150.

wars.name: Cham invasion of the Khmer Empire
wars.outcome: A Cham land invasion in 1170 was inconclusive; in 1177 a Cham fleet sacked Yasodharapura and killed the king, and the Cham occupied Cambodia for about four years until Jayavarman VII's naval victory in 1181.

wars.name: Jayavarman VII's conquest of Champa
wars.outcome: Vijaya was occupied in 1190-1191, then invaded in 1192, 1195, 1198-1199 and 1201-1203; Champa became a Khmer province under a puppet government in 1203 and the Khmer withdrew in 1220.

wars.name: Ayutthaya's sieges of Angkor (1352-1357)
wars.outcome: Uthong besieged Angkor in 1352 and took it in 1353; Siamese princes ruled until Suryavamsa Rajadhiraja retook the throne in 1357.

wars.name: Ayutthaya's siege and capture of Angkor (1393-1394)
wars.outcome: Ramesuan besieged Angkor in 1393 and captured it in 1394; the page does not say how it was recovered.

wars.name: Siege of Angkor (1431)
wars.outcome: Ponhea Yat abandoned Angkor as indefensible and moved to the Phnom Penh area; the Khmer Empire ends and Post-Angkor Cambodia begins.

certainty.note: Khmer frontiers were the reach of Angkor's governors and tributaries, not surveyed lines; the Cham coast, the Menam valley and the northern Mekong frontier are the softest.
